title: Research
text:
My research focuses on improving the quality and efficiency of survey data collection. I study how recruitment decisions affect who responds and how well survey findings reflect the population. I combine statistical methods, simulation studies, and computational tools to investigate these questions.
My collaborative research extends to health behavior, survey attitudes, and how people understand and evaluate public opinion polls.
University of Michigan, 2026
My dissertation investigates three ways to improve survey data collection: identifying groups that may benefit from different recruitment strategies; using predicted survey answers to help estimate participation; and using AI-generated profiles to prioritize recruitment.
The analyses for the three dissertation studies are complete, and manuscripts are being prepared for submission. Titles below are working titles.

title: Software
text:
I contribute to research software that makes computational methods accessible in everyday research practice.
ASReview LAB
Active learning for systematic reviews
ASReview LAB helps researchers screen large collections of titles and abstracts. It learns from screening decisions to prioritize records for further review.
My contributions include developing interfaces in React and REST APIs connecting the interface to Python servers, contributing to the first stable release, writing documentation, and improving usability through user feedback. I continued as a volunteer maintainer after my research-engineer appointment at Utrecht University.
View project ↗Star
ASReview-wordcloud
Exploring the text in review datasets
ASReview-wordcloud creates word-cloud visualizations from systematic review datasets, offering a quick impression of their textual content.
My work included processing dataset metadata in Python and developing visualizations of titles and abstracts.
View project ↗Star

title: About
text:
I am a social science methodologist and statistician working at the intersection of survey research, computational social science, and artificial intelligence. I earned my Ph.D. in Survey and Data Science from the University of Michigan in 2026.
My research asks how we can collect informative social data with limited resources. I develop methods for identifying groups that need different recruitment approaches, understanding who participates in surveys, and using AI to support data collection decisions. My collaborative work also examines health behavior, attitudes toward surveys, and public understanding of polls.
Alongside my research, I contribute to open-source software. As a research engineer at Utrecht University, I developed interfaces and supporting infrastructure for ASReview LAB, which uses active learning to assist systematic reviewing. I continued contributing as a volunteer maintainer after that appointment.
